- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- In early horizon (e.g., 30d), model underestimates mean reversion; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% relative to recent high.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags; add 0.3–0.7% buffer to forecast to capture momentum.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misses direction; align forecast with sentiment direction if >0.5 sentiment.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high; if last 3–5 days show no trend, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid false breakout.
